title: How John Hammond worked and why he is unrecognized
summary: Jones describes Hammond starting many projects at once and setting up recording dates, and he and Hinton ask why the public does not know his role.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Yes. Now you must remember, when John came out to Kansas City at that particular time, John was perhaps involved in about 20 or 30 different individual projects with different peoples that we were later to meet. Now when John would start a project and get somebody to put in the head of the project, he's gone, he's doing something else. Now when he comes back, Milt, if it's not done that's not his fault. Because remember we're dealing with individuals. We got individuals that's got individual problems. We're dealing with individuals, you know how it is, that when you say the recording date's at 1 o'clock they don't show up till 2:30. They come up with individual

problems; they come up with some excuses. But John at that particular time was staying in the Village and he don't live with these people. He'd just come 'round, "Hi fellows. What are you into?" He put up the projects, he set up the dates, he set up recording dates, as I have here all these dates for Miss Billie Holiday. All the dates that you see in here, he's the one that got the musicians.

What I've wondered about, Jo, as instrumental as this man has been, as monumental as he has been in the promotion and preservation of this great American art form, jazz, and which touched we the players know about and has each one of us in some sort of way. I know my first record date as a soloist in Cab Calloway's band - this man convinced Cab Calloway to use a bass as a solo, to use a drum as a solo with Cozy and with Chu Berry The American public I don't really think -
-do not know. Why should this be?
I mean the writers, the people that write about it - they wouldn't have anything to write about -

But every writer that's got a nice home, that's drawing a good salary - they say John is rich and what have you. He wasn't supposed to reach in his pocket like a Rockefeller. You're supposed to take your own talent.
